previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis, bladder and prostate cancer status post cystectomy with ileal conduit, and chronic substance use was admitted for altered mental status and reported hematemesis. He was found with a colostomy bag off and reported multiple falls, though imaging showed no acute intracranial abnormalities. Urine toxicology was positive for oxycodone and opiates, indicating intoxication as the likely cause of altered mental status. His hemoglobin dropped from 9.7 to 8.4 g/dL during the admission, reflecting worsening anemia. A chest X-ray showed mild pulmonary congestion and bibasilar opacities. Urine culture grew E. coli and Enterococcus, but due to chronic colonization from urinary diversions, antibiotics were withheld. The patient left against medical advice on the second hospital day after being counseled on the risks, including potential death from ongoing substance use and severe anemia. He was advised to continue home medications and follow up with his primary care provider.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ with HCV and EtOH cirrhosis presenting with melena and
hemtochezia.  Assess with dopplers: eval for ascites and portal vein
thrombosis

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler ultrasound images of the
abdomen were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal ultrasound ___
Abdominal ultrasound ___

FINDINGS: 

The liver appears diffusely coarsened and nodular consistent with known
cirrhosis.  No focal liver lesions are identified. There is no ascites. There
is no splenomegaly, with the spleen measuring 10.9 cm.  There is no
intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CHD measures 2 mm. There is no evidence of
stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.
The TIPS is patent and demonstrates wall-to-wall flow.
Portal vein and intra-TIPS velocities are as follows:
Main portal vein: 39.1 cm/sec, previously 60.7 cm/sec
Proximal TIPS: 104 cm/sec, previously 149cm/sec
Mid TIPS: 100 cm/sec, previously 161 cm/sec
Distal TIPS: 127  cm/sec, previously 159 cm/sec

Appropriate flow is seen in the hepatic veins and IVC.

PANCREAS: The imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits,
without masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic
tail obscured by overlying bowel gas.

KIDNEYS:  The right kidney measures 9.5 cm, the left kidney measures 9.5. 
Mild left renal fullness with a left percutaneous nephrostomy tube is noted. 
The right kidney is grossly unremarkable.


RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of the IVC is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Cirrhotic appearing liver without ascites or splenomegaly.
2.  Patent TIPS.
3.  Mild left renal fullness with left renal percutaneous nephrostomy.
